claims.text: Partial substitution of transition-metal elements can tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Partial substitution of transition-metal elements can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Transition-metal substitution modulates magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Fe, Mn, or Ni can serve as dopants for systematic tuning of a baseline non-equiatomic HEA composition.
Non-equiatomic HEA films can be fabricated by magnetron sputtering and subsequently annealed at 800–900 °C.
Annealing at 800–900 °C stabilizes the microstructure of the proposed HEA films.
Dopant incorporation changes local lattice distortions in the HEA.
Dopant incorporation changes site occupancy in the HEA.
Dopant-induced changes in lattice distortion and site occupancy affect superexchange pathways.
Doping changes the local atomic environment and alters the balance between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic exchange interactions.
Changes in the balance of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions reshape the magnetocaloric response.
Moderate doping levels will shift the Curie temperature.
Moderate doping levels will measurably change the magnetocaloric effect near room temperature.
The proposed doping strategy enables tunable magnetic-refrigeration properties.
The magnitude of the tuning effect depends on dopant solubility and spatial distribution.
Excessive doping may cause phase separation or reduced compositional homogeneity.
Phase separation or reduced homogeneity may limit the magnetic and magnetocaloric tuning effect.
